requirements.quote:
A server accepts 0-RTT by sending an early_data extension in the
   EncryptedExtensions
requirements.required_behavior: Send an early_data extension in EncryptedExtensions to signal acceptance.
requirements.why_checkable: The server's EncryptedExtensions can be decoded to verify the presence of early_data when 0-RTT is accepted.

requirements.quote:
The server then
   processes and acknowledges the 0-RTT packets that it receives.
requirements.condition: After a server accepts 0-RTT and receives a 0-RTT packet
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send valid 0-RTT data after acceptance and observe whether it reaches server processing.

requirements.quote:
The server then
   processes and acknowledges the 0-RTT packets that it receives.
requirements.condition: After a server accepts 0-RTT and receives a 0-RTT packet
requirements.why_checkable: A packet trace can verify that accepted 0-RTT packets are covered by acknowledgments from the server.

requirements.quote:
A server rejects 0-RTT by sending the EncryptedExtensions without an
   early_data extension.
requirements.required_behavior: Send EncryptedExtensions without an early_data extension to signal rejection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include an early_data extension in the rejecting EncryptedExtensions.
requirements.why_checkable: The rejecting EncryptedExtensions can be decoded to verify that early_data is absent.

requirements.quote:
A server will always reject 0-RTT if it sends
   a TLS HelloRetryRequest.
requirements.condition: When a server sends a TLS HelloRetryRequest
requirements.why_checkable: A handshake test can cause HelloRetryRequest and observe the server's resulting 0-RTT acceptance state.

requirements.quote:
When rejecting 0-RTT, a server MUST NOT
   process any 0-RTT packets, even if it could.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Process any 0-RTT packet, including one that is otherwise decryptable or processable.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can supply decryptable 0-RTT packets on a rejecting handshake and verify that no application or protocol processing occurs.

requirements.quote:
When 0-RTT was
   rejected, a client SHOULD treat receipt of an acknowledgment for a
   0-RTT packet as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, if it
   is able to detect the condition.
requirements.condition: When 0-RTT was rejected and the client can detect receipt of an acknowledgment for a 0-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the acknowledgment as a connection error.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continue the connection as though the acknowledgment were valid for rejected 0-RTT.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can reject 0-RTT, inject an acknowledgment covering a 0-RTT packet, and inspect the client's connection error code.

requirements.quote:
When 0-RTT is rejected, all connection characteristics that the
   client assumed might be incorrect.  This includes the choice of
   application protocol, transport parameters, and any application
   configuration.  The client therefore MUST reset the state of all
   streams
requirements.required_behavior: Reset the state of every stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retain a stream's pre-rejection state as active state.
requirements.why_checkable: A client test can create multiple streams before rejection and verify that each stream state is reset afterward.

requirements.quote:
The client therefore MUST reset the state of all
   streams, including application state bound to those streams.
requirements.condition: When 0-RTT is rejected and application state is bound to a stream
requirements.required_behavior: Reset the application state bound to that stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retain the bound application state from before rejection.
requirements.why_checkable: A client test can bind observable application state to 0-RTT streams and verify that rejection clears or reinitializes it.

requirements.quote:
A client MAY reattempt 0-RTT if it receives a Retry or Version
   Negotiation packet.  These packets do not signify rejection of 0-RTT.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a Retry packet during a 0-RTT attempt
requirements.required_behavior: Do not interpret the Retry packet itself as rejection of 0-RTT.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Mark 0-RTT rejected solely because the Retry packet was received.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-machine test can inject Retry and inspect whether the client records a 0-RTT rejection event solely from that packet.

requirements.quote:
A client MAY reattempt 0-RTT if it receives a Retry or Version
   Negotiation packet.  These packets do not signify rejection of 0-RTT.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a Version Negotiation packet during a 0-RTT attempt
requirements.required_behavior: Do not interpret the Version Negotiation packet itself as rejection of 0-RTT.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Mark 0-RTT rejected solely because the Version Negotiation packet was received.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-machine test can inject Version Negotiation and inspect whether the client records a 0-RTT rejection event solely from that packet.
